newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Experts welcome Lithuania move on nuclear safety.
newsitem.headline: Experts welcome Lithuania move on nuclear safety.

text.p: An international nuclear safety panel on Tuesday said it was satisfed with a Lithuanian government decision to follow safety recommendations at the Ignalina nuclear power plant.
The plant has the largest of the Chernobyl-type RBMK reactors, one of which in 1984 caused the world's worst nuclear disaster.
The reactors have to be shut down every year for routine maintenance and the panel asked the Lithuanians to keep them shut until vital safety upgrades were made.

"We were very satisfied to learn that the Lithuanian government is very much determined to follow all the recommendations made by our panel as well as other groups," Adolf Birkhofer, the panel's head, told Reuters.
"We were impressed that the problems we mentioned will be addressed before the reactors are restarted after their annual maintenance," he said.
One of the reactors is now shut for maintenance.
Birkhofer said the plant's management now had a greater commitment to safety at the plant.
The main problems include the reliablity of the shut-down system and in verification the reactors can carry the loads imposed on them.
